name: Sultan Hasanuddin International Airport
before:
The main gateway to eastern Indonesia, and the largest airport in that half of the country. It sits on the boundary between Makassar and Maros, about 20 km and fifteen minutes from the city centre by tollway, or 23 km and twenty minutes on the ordinary road.

Its value is as a connecting point. Flights run west to Jakarta, Surabaya, Denpasar and Balikpapan and east to Ambon, Ternate, Sorong and Jayapura, with international services to Singapore and Malaysia. It is also one of the main departure points for Hajj pilgrims from eastern Indonesia, with seasonal flights to Jeddah and Medina, so those weeks are busy.

The current terminal opened in August 2008 about 2 km south of the old one, built alongside an 11.47 km extension of the Ujung Pandang Tollway that improved access to both the city and the Port of Makassar.

It is also a major air force base, home to four Indonesian Air Force squadrons, so military aircraft are a normal sight.

The airport is named after Sultan Hasanuddin, the Sultan of Gowa who resisted the Dutch East India Company in the 1660s.
after:
Makassar's airport and a major connecting point between western and eastern Indonesia. It sits in Maros Regency on the boundary with Makassar, about 20 km from the city centre.

Flights run west to Jakarta, Surabaya, Denpasar and Balikpapan and east to Ambon, Ternate, Sorong and Jayapura, with international flights to Singapore, Kuala Lumpur and Jeddah. It is also the Hajj departure point for pilgrims from much of Sulawesi and Maluku, so the pilgrimage weeks are busy.

Its current terminal, about 2 km from the old one, opened in August 2008 and was greatly enlarged in June 2024.

Military aircraft are a normal sight: the Indonesian Air Force also flies from here, Sukhoi fighters included.

The airport is named after Sultan Hasanuddin.

claims.claim: Makassar's airport and a major connecting point between western and eastern Indonesia
claims.inAfter: Makassar's airport and a major connecting point between western and eastern Indonesia.
claims.note: Was 'The main gateway to eastern Indonesia' ('gateway to' is also a banned phrase). Wikipedia calls it a key hub connecting western and eastern Indonesia; Antara's report of the 2008 opening calls it the connecting gate to the other cities of eastern Indonesia. For the network today, the regulator's live route list for the airport has flights west to Soekarno-Hatta (Jakarta), Juanda (Surabaya) and I Gusti Ngurah Rai (Bali) and east to Pattimura (Ambon), Sentani (Jayapura), Domine Eduard Osok (Sorong), Mozes Kilangin (Timika) and many more.

claims.claim: in Maros Regency on the boundary with Makassar
claims.inAfter: It sits in Maros Regency on the boundary with Makassar
claims.note: Was 'on the boundary between Makassar and Maros'. The regulator places the airport in Mandai district of Maros Regency, and Antara's August 2026 reports put it in Maros Regency; Maros News says most of the airport is in Mandai, Maros, with only a small part inside Makassar city. So it is in Maros, on the Makassar boundary.

claims.note: The regulator's live route list names the airports: Soekarno-Hatta (Jakarta), Juanda (Surabaya), I Gusti Ngurah Rai (Denpasar), Sultan Aji Muhammad Sulaiman (Balikpapan), Pattimura (Ambon), Sultan Babullah (Ternate), Domine Eduard Osok (Sorong) and Sentani (Jayapura). claims.claim: international flights to Singapore, Kuala Lumpur and Jeddah
claims.inAfter: with international flights to Singapore, Kuala Lumpur and Jeddah
claims.note: Was 'international services to Singapore and Malaysia', with Jeddah and Medina given only as seasonal Hajj flights. Jeddah is now a regular route: Antara (13 November 2025) reports flyadeal's first Makassar to Jeddah flight, a regular weekly service, making six airlines on international routes (AirAsia, Malaysia Airlines, Garuda Indonesia, Lion Air, Scoot and flyadeal), and the regulator's live list has Lion Air to King Abdulaziz (Jeddah) as well as Scoot to Changi (Singapore) and AirAsia and Malaysia Airlines to Kuala Lumpur. Medina is not in the regulator's list, so it goes.

claims.claim: the Hajj departure point for pilgrims from much of Sulawesi and Maluku
claims.inAfter: It is also the Hajj departure point for pilgrims from much of Sulawesi and Maluku
claims.note: Was 'one of the main departure points for Hajj pilgrims from eastern Indonesia, with seasonal flights to Jeddah and Medina'. Antara (2 June 2026): the Makassar embarkation planned to send 16,728 pilgrims and staff in 2026, with pilgrims from South, West and Southeast Sulawesi, North Maluku and Maluku, and they came home through this airport. The flight destinations are dropped because Jeddah is now year-round (above) and the 2026 report does not name them.

claims.inAfter: current terminal, about 2 km from the old one, opened in August 2008
claims.note: detik (4 August 2008): the operator moved all its work to the new airport that morning, about 2 km from the old one. Antara: fully in operation since 4 August 2008, inaugurated by the president on 26 September 2008. Wikipedia's 'south' of the old one rests on it alone, so the direction goes.

claims.claim: the terminal was greatly enlarged in June 2024
claims.inAfter: and was greatly enlarged in June 2024
claims.note: The old text stopped at 2008. Wikipedia: the expansion, to triple the terminal from 50,000 to 150,000 m2, opened on 26 June 2024. detik (25 June 2024): the operator was moving departures from the old terminal into the new one from 26 June. Which parts of the building each flow uses now is not in any source from the last 12 months, so the text does not say.

The expanded terminal was completed and officially opened to the public on 26 June 2024.

claims.claim: the Indonesian Air Force also flies from here, Sukhoi fighters included
claims.inAfter: the Indonesian Air Force also flies from here, Sukhoi fighters included
claims.note: Was 'a major air force base, home to four Indonesian Air Force squadrons'. Antara (24 August 2026): an Air Force Sukhoi Su-30MK2 overran runway 13 on a test flight after an overhaul, and commercial flights carried on using runway 03/21; Antara's 2008 report has the president landing at the Sultan Hasanuddin Air Force base (Pangkalan TNI AU). The four squadrons rest on Wikipedia alone.
